newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Dec 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Dec 5.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Thursday:
- U.N. Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali said he was suspending his candidacy for re-election "for the time being" but not dropping out completely.

- Military logs for an eight-day period in which thousands of American troops might have been exposed to nerve gas shortly after the Persian Gulf war appear to have been removed or lost, according to the Pentagon.
- President Clinton is still wrestling with his choices for his national security team. Madeleine K. Albright is the leading candidate for Secretary of State.

- New York City schools chancellor Rudy Crew proposed the adoption of national education standards that would change what school children are expected to learn and how their achievement would be measured.

- Owners of the Connecticut Yankee nuclear power plant in Haddam Neck, which has one of the best performance records in the nuclear industry, decided to permanently shut it down, citing increased competition and high operating costs.
